family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
source: Arno, James C. 2007. Shughni: Phonology—consonant/vowel inventories; syllable structure. 28 March 2007.
claim: The three-page source is explicitly scoped to Shughni consonant and vowel inventories, positional consonant examples, and syllable structure.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: The consonant chart distinguishes bilabial, labiodental, dental, alveolar, postalveolar, palatal, velar and uvular places across stops, fricatives, affricates, glides/liquids and nasals.
source_forms: p b t d k g q; f v θ đ s z; source-encoded postalveolar/palatal/velar/uvular fricatives and affricates; w l y r m n ŋ

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: The inventory includes a voiceless uvular stop /q/ in addition to velar /k g/.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: The nasal inventory includes /m n ŋ/; the positional list illustrates /ŋ/ medially and finally but gives no initial example, so the file preserves this only as attested distribution rather than a categorical initial ban.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: The source distinguishes a set of long vowels from short vowels in its vowel-space diagram and includes central and front/back qualities beyond a five-vowel system.
source_forms: i u I e (Ə) o ε ʌ (ò) ö æ a; diagram distinguishes long vs short sets

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: Quoting Payne (1989), the handout characterizes long vowels as stable while short vowels—especially i and u—show wide allophonic variation; sample alternants are provided for 'moon' and 'he'.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
section: Word List (consonants): Initial, Medial, Final Positions
claim: The handout supplies consonant-by-consonant lexical examples in initial, medial and final positions, explicitly marking cells for which it provides no example; these entries are evidence of attestation, not proof of impossible positions.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: Attested syllable formats listed by the source are CV, CVC, CVCC, CVCCC, CCVC, V, VC and VCC.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: The listed CVCC, CVCCC and VCC formats establish attested complex codas, including three-consonant codas after a vowel in the handout's syllabification.

family: Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Iranian > Eastern Iranian > Pamir
claim: CCVC is explicitly listed, establishing attested two-consonant onsets in the source's syllable analysis.
